Terns body mass analysis

Atlit Common Tern & Little Tern ringing data - issue #5

2026-09-08

1 Background

The paper is investigating what drives Little Tern breeding-success collapse at Atlit, alongside the rise in Common Tern numbers. One candidate factor is adult body condition (mass). This report builds and compares three versions of a yearly, per-species mass metric from the raw ringing database (data_raw/ringing_data_raw.xlsx, 66k+ individual records, local-only/not in git - see data_raw/README.md):

  1. Spring (pre-breeding) mass - the metric that reproduces Yosef’s original hirMASS/albMASS columns (issue #5, task 1).
  2. Breeding-season mass - restricted to June-July and to adults, as a proxy for actual Atlit breeders rather than passage migrants (issue #5, task 2).
  3. Confirmed-breeder spring mass - a refinement of (1): spring-caught adults restricted further to individuals also encountered in June or July of the same year, i.e. more confident they stayed to breed at Atlit rather than just stopping over. Compared statistically against the full spring cohort.

This supersedes scripts/02_reverse_engineer_mass.R and scripts/03_breeding_mass.R, consolidated here so all three metrics and their comparisons are in one knittable report.

2 Data loading

raw_dir <- "../data_raw"
if (!dir.exists(raw_dir)) raw_dir <- "data_raw"
stopifnot(dir.exists(raw_dir))

proc_dir <- "../data_processed"
if (!dir.exists(proc_dir)) proc_dir <- "data_processed"

out_dir <- "../output"
if (!dir.exists(out_dir)) out_dir <- "output"

ringing_path <- file.path(raw_dir, "ringing_data_raw.xlsx")
stopifnot(file.exists(ringing_path))

# The sheet has a 2-row merged header with duplicate leaf names (two "Date"
# columns, two "CR" columns), which readxl's auto name-repair mangles
# unpredictably. Skip both header rows and assign names explicitly, using
# the column mapping verified against data_raw/README.md. The leading "#"
# column (col 1 in the spreadsheet) is entirely empty and readxl drops it
# outright, so the real data is 47 columns, not 48.
col_names_47 <- c(
  "CR1","RingReplace","Rec","RingPrefix","RingNum","Species","Sex","Age","Wing","Weight",
  "Date","Time","Place","Lat","Lon","Ringer","Country","Remarks","Net","CR2","Subsp","Tail","Head",
  "Breeding","CP1","CP2","CP3","CP4","Colour","D","M","OrigDate","OrigCountry","OrigLat","OrigLon","OrigAge",
  "OldCR1","OldCR2","OldCR3","OldMetal1","OldMetal2","OilHead","OilWings","OilUpperP","OilUnderP","OilLegs","OilSum"
)
raw <- read_excel(ringing_path, sheet = "Data", skip = 2, col_names = col_names_47)

# EURING age codes present in this sheet: 1 = pullus (nestling), 3 = this
# calendar year juvenile (this season's fledgling); 4/5/6 and the two-digit
# known-exact-hatch-year codes (14, 22, 25, 28, 29, 35, 37...) are all
# adults (terns can live ~20 years, extending the scale for known-age
# birds - confirmed with Inbal).
juvenile_ages <- c(1, 3)

terns <- raw %>%
  filter(Species %in% c("STEALB", "STEHIR")) %>%
  mutate(
    year = year(Date),
    month = month(Date),
    ring_id = paste0(trimws(RingPrefix), RingNum),
    is_new = is.na(Rec) | trimws(Rec) == "",
    is_adult = !(Age %in% juvenile_ages)
  )

cat("Total tern records:", nrow(terns), "| distinct individuals (ring_id):", n_distinct(terns$ring_id), "\n")
## Total tern records: 65934 | distinct individuals (ring_id): 18643

Caveat: ring_id (RingPrefix+RingNum) identifies an individual by its physical ring. 1383 records across the whole sheet are flagged RingReplace (ring physically replaced) - for those individuals, matching by ring_id across records breaks at the replacement point. Not corrected for here; a source of (probably small) undercount in the matching used in the “confirmed breeder” section below.

3 Task 1: Spring (pre-breeding) mass

Hypothesis (confirmed in a prior session): hirMASS/albMASS = mean Weight of new (non-recapture) individuals caught in spring (March-May), per species per year.

spring_records <- terns %>%
  filter(is_new, !is.na(Weight), month %in% 3:5)

spring_mass <- spring_records %>%
  group_by(year, Species) %>%
  summarise(mean_weight = mean(Weight), sd_weight = sd(Weight), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(Species, year)

3.1 Validation against the known legacy values (2012-2020)

legacy1 <- read.csv(file.path(raw_dir, "data1_2012-2020_legacy.csv"))
known <- legacy1 %>%
  select(year, hirMASS, albMASS) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(hirMASS, albMASS), names_to = "species_col", values_to = "reported_mass") %>%
  mutate(Species = ifelse(species_col == "hirMASS", "STEHIR", "STEALB"))

validation <- known %>%
  left_join(spring_mass, by = c("year", "Species")) %>%
  mutate(diff = mean_weight - reported_mass) %>%
  arrange(Species, year)

4 Task 2: Breeding-season (June-July, adults only) mass

Discovery (not obvious from the task’s wording, confirmed with Inbal before implementing): a naive “new individuals caught in June-July” filter is dominated by this-year chicks/juveniles, since chicks are ringed in the nest/shortly after fledging throughout the breeding season - not by adults. This must be filtered out or the metric mostly tracks fledgling weight, not adult condition.

age_month_evidence <- terns %>%
  filter(is_new, month %in% 6:7) %>%
  count(Species, month, Age) %>%
  arrange(Species, month, desc(n)) %>%
  group_by(Species, month) %>%
  slice_max(n, n = 3) %>%
  ungroup()

kable(age_month_evidence, caption = "Top age codes by count, new individuals, Jun/Jul (age 1 = pullus, 3 = this-year juvenile - both excluded below)")

spring_vs_breeding <- spring_mass %>%
  rename(spring_mean = mean_weight, spring_n = n) %>%

      select(year, Species, breeding_mean, breeding_n),
    by = c("year", "Species")

  mutate(diff = breeding_mean - spring_mean) %>%

4.1.1 Year-level pattern

for (sp in c("STEHIR", "STEALB")) {
  sub <- spring_vs_breeding %>% filter(Species == sp, !is.na(spring_mean), !is.na(breeding_mean))
  r <- cor(sub$spring_mean, sub$breeding_mean)
  cat("**", sp, "**: correlation (spring vs. breeding) = ", round(r, 3),
      ", mean difference (breeding - spring) = ", round(mean(sub$diff), 2), " g\n\n", sep = "")
}

STEHIR: correlation (spring vs. breeding) = -0.034, mean difference (breeding - spring) = -7.78 g

STEALB: correlation (spring vs. breeding) = 0.569, mean difference (breeding - spring) = -2.29 g

4.1.2 Significance test (individual-level)

The year-level correlation/difference above summarises the pattern across years, but doesn’t test whether spring and breeding-season weights actually differ. spring_records and breeding_records are built from disjoint ringing events (a bird’s first-ever ringing record can only be “new” once - see is_new in the Data loading section), so these are independent samples of individuals, suitable for a two-sample test:

for (sp in c("STEHIR", "STEALB")) {
  spring_w <- spring_records %>% filter(Species == sp) %>% pull(Weight)
  breeding_w <- breeding_records %>% filter(Species == sp) %>% pull(Weight)
  tt <- t.test(spring_w, breeding_w)
  wt <- wilcox.test(spring_w, breeding_w)
  cat("**", sp, "**: spring n=", length(spring_w), ", mean=", round(mean(spring_w), 2),
      "g; breeding n=", length(breeding_w), ", mean=", round(mean(breeding_w), 2),
      "g; Welch t-test p=", signif(tt$p.value, 3),
      ", Wilcoxon p=", signif(wt$p.value, 3), "\n\n", sep = "")
}

STEHIR: spring n=1828, mean=122.36g; breeding n=1117, mean=114.79g; Welch t-test p=5.2e-86, Wilcoxon p=2.44e-77

STEALB: spring n=309, mean=46.5g; breeding n=565, mean=44.68g; Welch t-test p=5.69e-11, Wilcoxon p=3.59e-12

Year-controlled robustness check - as in task 2b, a pooled comparison across years can be confounded if spring/breeding records happen to cluster in different years. This model holds year fixed while estimating the breeding-vs-spring effect:

for (sp in c("STEHIR", "STEALB")) {
  d <- bind_rows(
    spring_records %>% filter(Species == sp) %>% mutate(period = "spring"),
    breeding_records %>% filter(Species == sp) %>% mutate(period = "breeding")
  ) %>%
    mutate(year = factor(year), period = factor(period, levels = c("spring", "breeding")))
  m <- lm(Weight ~ period + year, data = d)
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients
  row <- co[grepl("^period", rownames(co)), , drop = FALSE]
  cat("**", sp, "** (year-controlled): breeding-vs-spring effect = ",
      round(row[1, "Estimate"], 2), " g (SE ", round(row[1, "Std. Error"], 2),
      "), p = ", signif(row[1, "Pr(>|t|)"], 3), "\n\n", sep = "")
}

STEHIR (year-controlled): breeding-vs-spring effect = -8.08 g (SE 0.42), p = 3.71e-79

STEALB (year-controlled): breeding-vs-spring effect = -2 g (SE 0.28), p = 3.62e-12

spring_vs_breeding %>%
  select(year, Species, spring_mean, breeding_mean) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(spring_mean, breeding_mean), names_to = "period", values_to = "mean_weight") %>%
  filter(!is.na(mean_weight)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(year, mean_weight, color = period)) +
  geom_line() + geom_point() +
  facet_wrap(~Species, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(title = "Spring vs. breeding-season mean mass", y = "Mean weight (g)") +
  theme_minimal()

Breeding-season adults weigh consistently less than spring arrivals - plausibly the cost of incubation/chick-rearing.

5 Task 2b: Confirmed-breeder spring mass

Goal: check whether Yosef’s original spring mass parameter (task 1 - mean weight of all spring-caught adults, new ringings only) differs from the weight of the subset we’re more confident actually bred at Atlit that year. Approach: take any adult weighed in spring - a new ringing or an in-hand recapture, doesn’t matter which, just that it was caught and weighed in March-May - and flag it as a confirmed breeder if that same ring was also recorded (recapture or field resighting, weighed or not) in June or July of the same year.

This deliberately does NOT filter to is_new (unlike task 1’s spring metric) - a recaptured adult weighed again in spring is just as valid a spring-weight data point as a newly-ringed one for this comparison.

summer_presence <- terns %>%
  filter(month %in% 6:7) %>%
  distinct(ring_id, year) %>%
  mutate(seen_summer = TRUE)

spring_adults <- terns %>%
  filter(is_adult, !is.na(Weight), month %in% 3:5) %>%
  left_join(summer_presence, by = c("ring_id", "year")) %>%
  mutate(confirmed_breeder = coalesce(seen_summer, FALSE))

kable(spring_adults %>% count(Species, confirmed_breeder),
      caption = "Spring adults (new + recaptures): confirmed (seen again Jun/Jul same year) vs. not")

confirmed_summary <- spring_adults %>%
  group_by(Species, confirmed_breeder) %>%
  summarise(mean_weight = mean(Weight), sd_weight = sd(Weight), n = n(), .groups = "drop")

5.1 Significance tests

Two comparisons. Note “confirmed breeders” is no longer a strict subset of task 1’s “all spring individuals” cohort - task 1 is is_new-only (that’s how it reproduces Yosef’s hirMASS/albMASS), while confirmed breeders here can include recaptured adults too. So (a) compares confirmed breeders against Yosef’s original spring parameter as defined, and (b) is the cleaner apples-to-apples split within the broader (new+recapture) spring adult cohort built here:

(a) Confirmed breeders vs. Yosef’s original spring parameter (task 1’s is_new-only cohort, as originally computed - checks whether the breeder-confirmed subset differs from the parameter as Yosef defined it):

for (sp in c("STEHIR", "STEALB")) {
  confirmed_w <- spring_adults %>% filter(Species == sp, confirmed_breeder) %>% pull(Weight)
  all_spring_w <- spring_records %>% filter(Species == sp) %>% pull(Weight)
  tt <- t.test(confirmed_w, all_spring_w)
  cat("**", sp, "**: confirmed n=", length(confirmed_w), ", mean=", round(mean(confirmed_w), 2),
      "g; all-spring n=", length(all_spring_w), ", mean=", round(mean(all_spring_w), 2),
      "g; Welch t-test p=", signif(tt$p.value, 3), "\n\n", sep = "")
}

STEHIR: confirmed n=180, mean=117.13g; all-spring n=1828, mean=122.36g; Welch t-test p=3.48e-12

STEALB: confirmed n=86, mean=46.77g; all-spring n=309, mean=46.5g; Welch t-test p=0.623

(b) Confirmed vs. unconfirmed spring adults (non-overlapping groups - the cleaner comparison, isolating “stayed” vs. “didn’t stay” among adults):

for (sp in c("STEHIR", "STEALB")) {
  confirmed_w <- spring_adults %>% filter(Species == sp, confirmed_breeder) %>% pull(Weight)
  unconfirmed_w <- spring_adults %>% filter(Species == sp, !confirmed_breeder) %>% pull(Weight)
  tt <- t.test(confirmed_w, unconfirmed_w)
  wt <- wilcox.test(confirmed_w, unconfirmed_w)
  cat("**", sp, "**: confirmed n=", length(confirmed_w), ", mean=", round(mean(confirmed_w), 2),
      "g; unconfirmed n=", length(unconfirmed_w), ", mean=", round(mean(unconfirmed_w), 2),
      "g; Welch t-test p=", signif(tt$p.value, 3),
      ", Wilcoxon p=", signif(wt$p.value, 3), "\n\n", sep = "")
}

STEHIR: confirmed n=180, mean=117.13g; unconfirmed n=1903, mean=122.53g; Welch t-test p=8.18e-13, Wilcoxon p=5.7e-12

STEALB: confirmed n=86, mean=46.77g; unconfirmed n=322, mean=46.24g; Welch t-test p=0.32, Wilcoxon p=0.529

(c) Year-controlled robustness check. Both groups’ weights vary by year, which could confound a naive pooled comparison if “confirmed” records happen to cluster in heavier- or lighter-than-average years. This model estimates the confirmed-breeder effect while holding year fixed:

for (sp in c("STEHIR", "STEALB")) {
  d <- spring_adults %>% filter(Species == sp) %>% mutate(year = factor(year))
  m <- lm(Weight ~ confirmed_breeder + year, data = d)
  co <- summary(m)$coefficients
  row <- co[grepl("confirmed_breeder", rownames(co)), , drop = FALSE]
  cat("**", sp, "** (year-controlled): confirmed-breeder effect = ",
      round(row[1, "Estimate"], 2), " g (SE ", round(row[1, "Std. Error"], 2),
      "), p = ", signif(row[1, "Pr(>|t|)"], 3), "\n\n", sep = "")
}

STEHIR (year-controlled): confirmed-breeder effect = -4.45 g (SE 0.8), p = 3.09e-08

STEALB (year-controlled): confirmed-breeder effect = 0.48 g (SE 0.49), p = 0.327

5.2 Interpretation

Read the three tests together per species rather than any single p-value: (a) and (b) tell you the raw pooled-across-years difference; (c) tells you whether that difference survives once year-to-year variation is accounted for. Small per-year sample sizes (see the per-year table above) mean this should be treated as an exploratory signal, not a final result, until Yosef/Inbal review sample sizes per group per year.

6 Save outputs

write.csv(spring_mass, file.path(proc_dir, "spring_mass_by_year_species.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(breeding_mass, file.path(proc_dir, "breeding_mass_by_year_species.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(
  spring_adults %>% select(ring_id, year, Species, Age, Weight, is_new, confirmed_breeder),
  file.path(proc_dir, "confirmed_breeder_spring_mass.csv"),
  row.names = FALSE
)

# ---- Update master_dataset_2010_2026.csv's hirMASS/albMASS columns -----
# Spring metric remains the single source for hirMASS/albMASS across all
# years (2011-2026), as established in the prior session - superseding
# data1.csv's 2012-2020-only values.
mass_wide <- spring_mass %>%
  mutate(col = ifelse(Species == "STEHIR", "hirMASS_new", "albMASS_new"),
         mean_weight = round(mean_weight, 1)) %>%
  select(year, col, mean_weight) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = col, values_from = mean_weight)

master_path <- file.path(proc_dir, "master_dataset_2010_2026.csv")
master <- read.csv(master_path) %>%
  select(-hirMASS, -albMASS) %>%
  left_join(mass_wide, by = "year") %>%
  rename(hirMASS = hirMASS_new, albMASS = albMASS_new)

write.csv(master, master_path, row.names = FALSE, na = "NA")
cat("Updated", master_path, "and wrote 3 CSVs to", proc_dir, "\n")
